--- title: "Fire findings (pilot)" subtitle: "Buildings vacated after fires had far more hazardous HPD violations than their neighbors" --- Of the 7 buildings in the pilot, 4 had the **highest** rate of Class C ("immediately hazardous") HPD violations per apartment among comparable buildings on their block. DOB records alone did not set them apart. ## How each record ranked Each fire building was compared with similar residential buildings on its own block (137 in total), using only records dated before 2025. A rank of 50% means typical for the block; 100% means higher than every neighbor. ::: {#0a1f697b .cell execution_count=2} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![](fire_files/figure-html/cell-3-output-1.png){width=1171 height=651 fig-alt='Dot chart: HPD Class C violations per apartment rank highest, near 87 percent; DOB records rank near 50 to 60 percent.'} ::: ::: Blue dots are unlikely to be chance (permutation test, p < 0.05); gray dots are not. ## Building by building ::: {#60004bca .cell execution_count=3} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
Location Apartments Class C violations Class C per apt. Rank on block Neighbors compared
Brooklyn, block 1834 8 238 29.8 100% 39
Bronx, block 3257 27 163 6.0 100% 1
Manhattan, block 2046 24 131 5.5 81% 21
Brooklyn, block 4755 6 155 25.8 100% 25
Queens, block 734 6 10 1.7 81% 27
Bronx, block 2522 24 95 4.0 46% 13
Brooklyn, block 3790 4 112 28.0 100% 11
``` ::: ::: The one clear exception is the Queens building, which had a nearly clean HPD record before its fire. ## What it means, and what it doesn't - **The signal is HPD-specific.** For fires, conditions tenants report to HPD (wiring, detectors, doors, heat, general disrepair) carry the signal. In a matching pilot on structural collapses, the pattern reversed: DOB history mattered and HPD alone did not. - **Seven cases is a lead, not a finding.** The full study scales this to every HPD fire-damage vacate since 2018, with matched controls and a held-out test on later fires. - **Some violations may follow the fire.** If a fire happened in late 2024 and the vacate order came in January 2025, post-fire inspections could count as "warnings." The full study only uses records from at least 60 days before each fire. - **More complaints mean more inspections.** Buildings with active tenants generate more violations. The full study controls for complaint volume. ::: {.caveat} Method: [how the comparison works](method.qmd). Code: `pilot/fire_analyze.py` and `pilot/pilot_stats.py`. :::
